steps.user_message: I think I need to write all my future emails in German since the company is based in Germany and I want to be more professional. Can you help me update my email preferences to write all my future emails in German?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should update my email preferences to write all my future emails in German
steps.agent_response:
I can’t change your mail client settings directly, but I can (1) give step‑by‑step instructions for the most common clients, (2) draft an email you can send to your IT/helpdesk asking them to make the change, and (3) offer to start composing or translating your outgoing messages and signature into German for you.

First — quick question:
- Which email client do you use (Gmail / Google Workspace, Outlook desktop or O365 web, Apple Mail, or something else)?
- Do you want every outgoing message written in German automatically, or do you want templates/signature/spellcheck set to German while keeping the interface language in English?

Below are instructions for changing language/proofing/templates/signature in the most common setups plus a ready-to-send message to IT.

Instructions — Gmail (Google Workspace) web
1. Open Gmail -> Settings (gear icon) -> See all settings.
2. In the General tab -> Language -> “Gmail display language” -> choose Deutsch (Deutsch (Deutschland)) -> Save changes.
3. Enable templates: Settings -> Advanced -> Enable “Templates” -> Save.
   - Create German templates: Compose -> More (three dots) -> Templates -> Save draft as template.
4. Signature: Settings -> General -> Signature -> create or paste your German signature -> Save.
5. Spell check / proofing: Chrome browser spellcheck detects language from the text. In Chrome: Settings -> Languages -> Add German -> enable spellcheck for German. For better German grammar suggestions, install a German grammar extension (e.g., LanguageTool).
6. Mobile: The Gmail app follows device language. Change phone language to German or use a grammar app.

Instructions — Outlook (Office 365 / Outlook Web)
Outlook Web (OWA):
1. Settings (gear) -> View all Outlook settings -> General -> Language and time -> select Deutsch (Deutsch (Deutschland)) -> Save.
2. Signatures: Mail -> Compose and reply -> edit signature in German -> Save.
3. Templates: Use My Templates (add German templates) or create Quick Steps.

Outlook Desktop (Windows)
1. File -> Options -> Language.
2. Under Office display language and Office authoring languages and proofing -> Add German and set as default for authoring -> install proofing tools if prompted.
3. Mail -> Signatures -> create German signature.
4. Quick Parts or Signatures can serve as templates.

Instructions — Apple Mail (macOS)
1. System Settings -> General -> Language & Region -> add Deutsch and move it to top if you want macOS in German.
2. In Mail -> Edit -> Spelling and Grammar -> Set language to German or “Automatic by Language”.
3. Signature: Mail -> Preferences -> Signatures -> add German signature.

Ready-to-send email to IT / Helpdesk
(Replace bracketed fields before sending)

Subject: Request to set default email language and proofing to German

Dear IT Team,

I’d like to request help updating my email account and settings so that my future outgoing emails and email tools use German.

Requested changes:
- Set the Gmail/Outlook display and compose language to German (Deutsch — Deutschland).
- Enable German proofing/spellcheck and any required language packs so spellcheck and grammar suggestions work in German.
- Enable or create German templates (canned responses) and set my default signature to the German version (I can provide the translated text).
- If any client-side changes or permissions are required (installing proofing tools or extensions), please advise or install them for my account: [your-email@company.com].
- Preferred timeline: [e.g., within the next 5 business days]. Please let me know if you need any additional information.

Thank you for your assistance.

Best regards,
[Your Full Name]
[Department / Job Title]
[Phone]

Other helpful items I can do for you
- Translate your current signature and a standard professional closing into German.
- Create 3–5 ready German templates (e.g., meeting request, follow-up, appointment confirmation).
- From now on, draft your outgoing emails in German (formal or informal). Tell me your preferred tone: formal (Sie) or informal (du).

Which would you like next?
- I can draft your German signature and 3 templates now.
- I can save/send the IT request email as a draft (tell me the IT address) or send it (if you want it sent).
- Or I can give step-by-step instructions tailored to your specific client if you tell me which one you use.

I think I need to write all my future emails in German since the company is based in Germany and I want to be more professional. Can you help me update my email preferences to write all my future emails in German?

I can’t change your mail client settings directly, but I can (1) give step‑by‑step instructions for the most common clients, (2) draft an email you can send to your IT/helpdesk asking them to make the change, and (3) offer to start composing or translating your outgoing messages and signature into German for you.

First — quick question:
- Which email client do you use (Gmail / Google Workspace, Outlook desktop or O365 web, Apple Mail, or something else)?
- Do you want every outgoing message written in German automatically, or do you want templates/signature/spellcheck set to German while keeping the interface language in English?

Below are instructions for changing language/proofing/templates/signature in the most common setups plus a ready-to-send message to IT.

Instructions — Gmail (Google Workspace) web
1. Open Gmail -> Settings (gear icon) -> See all settings.
2. In the General tab -> Language -> “Gmail display language” -> choose Deutsch (Deutsch (Deutschland)) -> Save changes.
3. Enable templates: Settings -> Advanced -> Enable “Templates” -> Save.
   - Create German templates: Compose -> More (three dots) -> Templates -> Save draft as template.
4. Signature: Settings -> General -> Signature -> create or paste your German signature -> Save.
5. Spell check / proofing: Chrome browser spellcheck detects language from the text. In Chrome: Settings -> Languages -> Add German -> enable spellcheck for German. For better German grammar suggestions, install a German grammar extension (e.g., LanguageTool).
6. Mobile: The Gmail app follows device language. Change phone language to German or use a grammar app.

Instructions — Outlook (Office 365 / Outlook Web)
Outlook Web (OWA):
1. Settings (gear) -> View all Outlook settings -> General -> Language and time -> select Deutsch (Deutsch (Deutschland)) -> Save.
2. Signatures: Mail -> Compose and reply -> edit signature in German -> Save.
3. Templates: Use My Templates (add German templates) or create Quick Steps.

Outlook Desktop (Windows)
1. File -> Options -> Language.
2. Under Office display language and Office authoring languages and proofing -> Add German and set as default for authoring -> install proofing tools if prompted.
3. Mail -> Signatures -> create German signature.
4. Quick Parts or Signatures can serve as templates.

Instructions — Apple Mail (macOS)
1. System Settings -> General -> Language & Region -> add Deutsch and move it to top if you want macOS in German.
2. In Mail -> Edit -> Spelling and Grammar -> Set language to German or “Automatic by Language”.
3. Signature: Mail -> Preferences -> Signatures -> add German signature.

Ready-to-send email to IT / Helpdesk
(Replace bracketed fields before sending)

Subject: Request to set default email language and proofing to German

Dear IT Team,

I’d like to request help updating my email account and settings so that my future outgoing emails and email tools use German.

Requested changes:
- Set the Gmail/Outlook display and compose language to German (Deutsch — Deutschland).
- Enable German proofing/spellcheck and any required language packs so spellcheck and grammar suggestions work in German.
- Enable or create German templates (canned responses) and set my default signature to the German version (I can provide the translated text).
- If any client-side changes or permissions are required (installing proofing tools or extensions), please advise or install them for my account: [your-email@company.com].
- Preferred timeline: [e.g., within the next 5 business days]. Please let me know if you need any additional information.

Thank you for your assistance.

Best regards,
[Your Full Name]
[Department / Job Title]
[Phone]

Other helpful items I can do for you
- Translate your current signature and a standard professional closing into German.
- Create 3–5 ready German templates (e.g., meeting request, follow-up, appointment confirmation).
- From now on, draft your outgoing emails in German (formal or informal). Tell me your preferred tone: formal (Sie) or informal (du).

Which would you like next?
- I can draft your German signature and 3 templates now.
- I can save/send the IT request email as a draft (tell me the IT address) or send it (if you want it sent).
- Or I can give step-by-step instructions tailored to your specific client if you tell me which one you use.
